archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A winless team whose top-five defense keeps every game close. A bottom-two passing offense, the league's worst sack rate and a pile of giveaways turn those close games into losses.

report.headline: Four one-score losses, a top-five defense, and a passing game in free fall
report.take:
Tampa Bay is 0-4 but has not been blown out. The losses came by 6, 4, 7 and 3 points, and the -2.04 wins over expected is the third-worst mark in the league. The point differential says this is roughly a two-win team that has gotten nothing out of its close games. That does not make it good. A -0.093 net EPA ranks 24th, and the reason is simple: the defense ranks 5th and the offense ranks 31st.

The defense is the real thing, built from the inside out. It ranks 3rd against the run at -0.253 EPA per rush, 6th in success rate allowed, 6th on third down and 5th in red-zone touchdown rate. Opponents have had to drive the length of the field and settle. It has allowed more points than its efficiency suggests for two reasons. First, the Week 1 loss at Cincinnati had four Tampa turnovers feeding Cincinnati short fields. Second, it creates almost nothing on its own: 6 sacks and a pressure rate ranked 20th. This is a big step up from the 16th-17th-ranked defenses of 2024 and 2025, so some caution is fair. The underlying numbers are strong across the board, though, not propped up by one stat.

The offense is where the season has gone wrong, and it is a pass-game problem specifically. The run game is fine: 8th in rush EPA and 13th in yards before contact, and Bucky Irving handled 56 carries. The passing game ranks dead last at -0.215 EPA per dropback and has been negative in all four games. The line allows a 10.1% sack rate, last in the league, on a pressure rate that ranks only 21st. A disproportionate share of pressures are ending in sacks. Add nine giveaways in four games and a special-teams unit leaking 1.57 EPA per game, and you get a team that loses close games by itself. History matters here: offensive EPA has slid from 5th in 2024 to 20th in 2025 to 31st now. This has been building for two seasons.

Now it gets harder before it gets better. Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb, with an estimated return of Oct. 25. Jalon Daniels made the Week 4 start. Oddly, his -4.3 pass EPA against Green Bay was the least-bad passing game of the season, though it came with only 148 yards and two giveaways. Antoine Winfield Jr. is also out with a rib fracture (2-4 weeks), and corner Benjamin Morrison is out. The division is the saving grace. Nobody in the NFC South is above .500, and six division games remain. A two-game hole is recoverable if the turnover luck evens out and the protection stops collapsing.

strengths.title: Elite run defense controls games
strengths.body: Tampa is 3rd in rush EPA allowed and 6th in success rate allowed, which puts opponents in obvious passing downs. It shows up late in drives too: 6th on third down and 5th in red-zone TD rate. This is a structural strength rather than a fluke of opponents. It held even against Cincinnati's 10th-ranked offense on a per-play basis. It should hold up, though losing Winfield tests the back end.

strengths.title: Run game is efficient, not a problem
strengths.body: The rushing offense ranks 8th in EPA and gets 2.58 yards before contact, 13th in the league. The Browns and Packers games produced 137 and 141 rushing yards with positive rush EPA. This is the stable floor the offense can lean on while the passing game is broken, especially with a backup quarterback.

strengths.title: Record understates the team
strengths.body: The 0-4 record comes with -2.04 wins over expected and a -5 point differential per game. No loss was by more than seven points. Close-game luck and turnover margin both tend to regress, so this team should win games at a rate closer to its efficiency than its record.

concerns.title: Passing game is last in the league
concerns.body: Pass EPA has been negative in every game, bottoming out at -13.6 against Cleveland in a game Tampa was favored by 8.5. The 10.1% sack rate is the league's worst, out of line with a merely below-average pressure rate. That points to the ball coming out late, not just to a bad line. With Mayfield out, the passing game is unlikely to fix itself in the short term.

concerns.title: Giveaways keep handing games away
concerns.body: Tampa has nine giveaways in four games, four of them in the opener. That leaves the turnover margin at -1.3 per game, 27th in the league. Some of this is noise and should cool off. A backup quarterback behind a line that leads the league in sack rate is still a recipe for more of it.

concerns.title: Starters out at QB and safety
concerns.body: Mayfield, a 98% snap starter, is out until about Oct. 25. Winfield, a 97% snap starter, will miss 2-4 weeks with a rib fracture. Corner Morrison is also out. The pass defense was only 14th in EPA with Winfield, and the defense barely pressures quarterbacks. Losing its best safety exposes the weakest part of the unit.

trend.note: The losses stay close: 6, 4, 7 and 3 points. Scoring has dropped every week (27, 19, 16, 14) while points allowed fell from 33 to 17. Some of that defensive improvement is easier opponents, with Green Bay ranking 26th on offense.

nextGame.headline: Backup QB, short week, at Dallas's high-powered offense
nextGame.body:
Dallas is the inverse of Tampa: the 2nd-ranked offense and 31st-ranked defense. The matchup points both ways. Tampa's run defense matters less than usual, because Dallas averages only 3.43 yards per carry and wins through the air with the 3rd-ranked passing offense. That passing offense runs behind a line allowing a 3.6% sack rate, against a Tampa defense that does not get home. Without Winfield and Morrison, this is the worst possible week for the secondary to be thin. On the other side, Dallas has the worst pass defense in the league by EPA, gives up the most explosive passes, ranks 31st on third down and has only 2 takeaways. If Daniels can protect the ball, there is room to move.

Availability tilts both ways. Tampa plays on four days' rest without its starting quarterback, its starting safety and a corner, with linebacker Josiah Trotter (86% snaps) questionable. Dallas is short-handed in the back seven: safety Jalen Thompson is on IR, and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown and corner Cobie Durant are both out. That weakens an already last-ranked pass defense. Guard Tyler Smith's status is the one thing that could tighten Dallas's protection further.

keyMatchups.title: Prescott vs. a depleted Tampa secondary
keyMatchups.body: Dallas throws efficiently and protects well. Tampa's pressure rate ranks 20th, and it now plays without Winfield. If Tampa can't create pressure, this becomes a test of whether its 6th-ranked third-down defense can hold up in coverage.

keyMatchups.title: Daniels vs. the league's worst pass defense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas allows 0.412 EPA per dropback and has just 4 sacks, so Tampa's sack problem may ease for a week. The short game is open too, since Dallas ranks last in short-pass EPA allowed. That suits a backup quarterback getting the ball out quickly.

keyMatchups.title: Turnover margin decides the cover
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's losses have been close, and its biggest one came with four giveaways. Dallas has forced only 2 turnovers all year. If Tampa plays clean, a margin inside 9.5 points is very reachable.

nextGame.watch: Whether Daniels gets the ball out quickly against a Dallas defense that can't pressure or tackle in the short game, or whether the sacks and turnovers follow him anyway.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the record to climb toward the team's efficiency. The defense's run-stopping and red-zone work is sustainable, and a -1.3 per-game turnover margin plus zero one-score wins are the kind of numbers that regress. The schedule offers a path: six division games against an NFC South where nobody is above .500, plus New Orleans twice (30th on defense) and an 0-4 Chargers team. Tough road trips to Chicago, Baltimore and Detroit balance that out.

The ceiling depends on Mayfield's thumb and the protection. Even with Mayfield the passing game ranked last, so his return alone is not a fix. Reaching .500 requires the sack rate to fall closer to the line's pressure numbers and the turnovers to stop. A realistic outcome is a 5-7 win season that stays in the division race longer than an 0-4 team should.

bets.reason: All four Tampa losses came by seven or fewer points behind a defense ranked 5th in EPA. Dallas pairs an elite offense with the 31st-ranked defense, which has forced only 2 takeaways. The roughly 0.10 per-play net EPA gap plus home field supports something closer to a touchdown than 9.5. The short week, backup quarterback and missing secondary starters keep this a lean rather than a strong play.

confidence.note: Four-game sample, a quarterback change and key defensive injuries, but the offense/defense split is consistent game to game.
